successCriteria.description: In docs/DOMAIN.md, the `LeaveRequestQueryParams` table's final row and the `balance` heading are on separate lines: the row reads exactly `| offset | number | false |`, followed by a blank line, followed by `## balance` on its own line. The string `| offset | number | false |## balance` no longer occurs anywhere in the file.

A heading-based section lookup for `balance` against docs/DOMAIN.md resolves and returns the balance section body (the `Balance` and `LeaveBalance` tables plus the `Represents leave balance data managed by the `balance` module...` description) — the section is addressable again, and the lookup does not fall back to the `leave` section.

constraints: The change is confined to docs/DOMAIN.md. No file under src/, web/, tests/, migrations/, seeds/, or scripts/ may be modified, and no test may be added or changed — this is a documentation-only repair of a line break.

The repair is whitespace-only: the `LeaveRequestQueryParams` table's eight rows and their cell contents, the `balance` heading text, and every other byte of docs/DOMAIN.md stay exactly as they are. No row, field, type, or description is added, removed, reordered, or reworded.

The restored heading must be a level-2 ATX heading (`## balance`) matching the file's existing top-level section headings (`## base`, `## leave`, `## employee`, `## policy`, `## notification`, `## audit`, `## validation`, `## system`, `## uptime`) — not a level-3 heading, not a setext heading, and not a bolded pseudo-heading.

The heading must be preceded by a blank line so the preceding table terminates; a heading immediately abutting a table row is not parsed as a heading by CommonMark and would leave the defect in place.

The fix must be made in place in docs/DOMAIN.md — not by regenerating the file, not by reordering sections, and not by relocating the `balance` content into another section. The `balance` section stays between the `leave` section and the `employee` section, in its current position.

No other known doc drift in docs/DOMAIN.md is to be corrected by this change. The stale `audit` section (documented as `Audit`/`AuditLog`/`AuditRecord`/`AuditServiceInterface` with `oldValues`/`newValues`/`performedBy`/`performedAt` while the built entity is `{ id, actorId, action, entityType, entityId, beforeState, afterState, occurredAt }`) and the stale `leave`/`employee` fields are explicitly recorded as pre-existing drift in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and are out of scope here.
outOfScope: Reconciling docs/DOMAIN.md's stale content with the built code — the `audit` section's `oldValues`/`newValues`/`performedBy`/`performedAt` fields, the `leave` section's `leaveTypeId`/`approvedBy`/`approvedAt`, and `EmploymentStatus.INACTIVE`. These are recorded as pre-existing, deliberately uncorrected drift in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

Adding, removing, or reordering any section, entity, table, or field in docs/DOMAIN.md, including documenting the `uptime`/`system` readiness entities or the `PendingDecision` projection beyond what the file already contains.
Introducing markdown linting, a heading-index generator, or any new CI check that would have caught this defect. The repair is the line break only; no tooling is added.
Any change to source, tests, migrations, seeds, or scripts, and any change to the leave pending-decisions / approver-notification feature this document edit accompanied.

ambiguities.description: Whether this phase should also add a regression guard (a markdown lint rule, a heading-index assertion, or a test) that fails when a section heading is ever collapsed onto a preceding line again, or whether the repair is the line break alone.
options: Line break only — no guard added (matches the intent's 'fix them in place' wording and the doc-only scope)
Add a lightweight guard in the same phase so the defect class cannot recur
Defer the guard to a separate follow-up phase

ambiguities.description: Whether the `balance` section's content should be reconciled with the built balance module while the section is being touched, or left byte-identical. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md records DOMAIN.md as stale relative to the architecture document, so a reader could reasonably expect the repair to also refresh the section.
options: Leave the section content byte-identical — restore addressability only (the drift is recorded as known and deliberately uncorrected)
Refresh the balance section's entities/fields to match the built module in the same change

entityInvariants.invariant: The `balance` section is a top-level, heading-addressable section: its heading occupies its own line, is preceded by a blank line, and is followed by the section's prose and tables. It is never merged into, or terminated by, a preceding table row. The section remains addressable by heading lookup for the lifetime of the file.

The table is a well-formed markdown table: every row, including the last (`| offset | number | false |`), is a complete line terminated by a newline, and no row carries trailing content from a following block. The table's row set and cell values are unchanged by this repair.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Heading-based section lookup against docs/DOMAIN.md (the `section` parameter of the readFile tool and any heading index built from the file)
interfaceConstraints.authRule: None — the document is read-only reference material with no access control.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: A lookup for `balance` must return the balance section body, not an empty result and not the preceding `leave` section. A lookup for any other existing top-level section (`base`, `leave`, `employee`, `policy`, `notification`, `audit`, `validation`, `system`, `uptime`) must keep returning exactly what it returned before this change — the repair must not shift, merge, or shadow any other section boundary.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The restored heading must follow the same top-level section convention already used throughout docs/DOMAIN.md: a level-2 ATX heading on its own line, preceded by a blank line, with the section's prose beginning on the following line. Match the existing `## leave` / `## employee` / `## policy` boundaries rather than inventing a new heading style.

The `balance` section's content must remain byte-identical to what it is now — the `Represents leave balance data managed by the `balance` module...` description, the `Balance` table, the `LeaveBalance` table, and the `Employee` / `LeavePolicy` relationship lines. Only the line break before the heading is restored; no content inside the section is touched.

The `LeaveRequestQueryParams` table's eight rows (`status`, `leaveTypeId`, `startDateFrom`, `startDateTo`, `endDateFrom`, `endDateTo`, `limit`, `offset`) and their `Field | Type | Required` values must match the table as it stands now, and must stay consistent with the `LeaveRequestQueryParams` type the leave module consumes — the repair changes no field, type, or requiredness.

The `balance` section's documented entities must stay consistent with the reconciled architecture's balance module (the `Balance` entity and the `balance` module boundary) — the repair restores addressability only and must not alter, add, or remove any documented balance entity or field.

The repair must not contradict the drift notes already recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, which state that docs/DOMAIN.md is stale relative to the architecture document and that the `audit` section drift is known and deliberately uncorrected. Restoring the `balance` heading is a formatting repair, not a reconciliation of DOMAIN.md's content with the architecture document.

integrationPoints.target: docs/DOMAIN.md heading structure (the `## balance` top-level section boundary)
integrationPoints.why: The file's top-level headings are the addressing scheme for every downstream consumer: the readFile `section` lookup, the heading index the architecture/context agents build, and the section-update path used to maintain the document. A collapsed heading silently removes the `balance` section from all of them, so the repair restores the addressing contract rather than just cosmetics.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md records the known drift between the two documents and points readers at DOMAIN.md sections by name. Those references assume DOMAIN.md's sections are addressable; the repair keeps that assumption true and must not alter the drift notes themselves.
